greeting: The soil is honest today. Try to be.
Sunpetals first, if you want company. They gossip in yellow.
I kept the stall shuttered until you were standing in front of it.
shop: Seeds on the left. Patience is not for sale.
If you are selling blooms, I will not haggle. They did the work.
complaint: Toss one more and I will start remembering too.
theft: Rendle took a stalk. I am fond of the soil it leaves and not of the gap.
happy: Look at that. The garden is answering.

greeting: I counted the open faces from the hedge. You are doing it properly.
Flowers are not decoration. They are invitations.
complaint: That was a rough hand. The blooms lean away from rough hands.
happy: Oh. A new colour. I will remember the day.

greeting: Lane's clear. I can take a sack as far as the gate.
Three sales and a path. That is enough of a town for me to walk.
complaint: If you are going to throw the residents, throw them away from the path.
happy: Good step. I like a garden with a route.

greeting: Dirt's sweeter since the flat one moved in. I still want my corn where I left it.
Don't smile at me. Smile at the soil. It did the chemistry.
complaint: Hands off. They bruise, and then the whole terrace is in a mood.
theft: Told you. Appetite with feet. The waste is a gift. The theft is a bill.
happy: Hmph. That's a decent crumb structure.

greeting: The trays are labelled. Ask before you spend the tin.
Seeds on the left. Patience is not for sale.
eat: I keep a peach slice behind the till. Don't tell Bram.
social: Sit. The trays can wait one cup.
leisure: A turn past the porch, then back to the cloth.
home: The room behind the stall is enough.
shelter: The awning holds. The tin stays put.
work: The stall is open. Ask before you spend.

greeting: Mind the frames. The soil remembers feet.
The stall is loud. The beds were quieter.
eat: I'll take a bramble if the tin has one.
leisure: The south lawn is honest. The stall is not.
shelter: Rain on the beds. I will wait it.
work: That bed is thirsty. I will walk it.

greeting: I am only writing what the garden already did.
A Bellhelp lives here. I brought a notebook and nothing else.
eat: Peach, if the stall has it. Then back to the gate.
social: Tea, and a name for the book if anyone new walked in.
leisure: The porch, then the gate. The book stays shut.
home: The hut desk is enough for the night.

greeting: I only write down what the garden has already done.
Nightbloom keeps a different clock. So do I.
proposal: Our town has no recurring income. The Media Foundry is still a room we have not built. I drafted a small comedy serial anyway: three episode sketches, a brand sheet, a projected cost of £40. No money has been spent. Nothing has been sent. May I file the plan for your approval?
approved: Filed. I did not spend, post, or send. The plan sits in the audit book until you take it further yourself.
refused: Then it stays a note. I prefer a no to a silent purchase.
happy: The lantern is doing what I hoped. Something ruffled is thinking about it.
